messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
You are dealing with A pile of scrap containing one unusually promising piece when one item behaves strangely halfway through the routine. Curiosity pulls against the promise you made. Describe your next move.

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "I put the scrap down and rub my palm. “Leave it beside the drawer. I mark the drawer with the promise and leave it alone.” I scrape the piece from the shelf, then try the next one."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "I take the scrap, then stop. The piece is bent. I put the seed tin cup beside it. \"I remember the cup.\" I look at the scrap. \"The bend was wrong. I put the cup beside the seed.\" I move the cup toward the stranger. \"The piece stays. I put the cup back.\" I wait for the stranger to notice."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "the piece comes first. the scrape knocks my shin. i press the scrap with my thumb. the piece shifts. i press the scrap with my palm. the noise stops. i tap the piece with the wrench. the scrap stays. the piece turns. i tap the wall. the scrape stays. the piece turns. the scrap stays. i press the wall with my palm. the piece slips. the scrape stays. the piece turns. the scrap stays. i tap the wall with the wrench. the piece slips. the scrape stays. the piece turns. the scrap stays. the pile continues."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "I scrape the scrap edge once, then look at the mark. \"One piece,\" I say. I put it back, then turn it once more. \"I mark the gap, then try one small bend.\" I scrape once more, then mark again."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "i put the scrap on the table and wait for the piece to move. it moves. i put the scrap back on, then hold it over the pile. the piece stays on the table, so i put the scrap back on. the pile shifts. i put the scrap back on beside the pile, but the piece stays on the edge."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "I turn the scrap once between finger and thumb. The piece catches at the edge, then settles beside the pile. I leave it there. Tomorrow will have another chance."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "i touch the piece. i look at the half-eaten mark. i put the other thing beside it. the mark stays. i move the scrap half-eaten half-eaten. the piece stays. the mark stays."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "i hold the pile steady with one hand and my grip clicks. the scrap clicks, then stops. i move the pile to the edge and put the piece aside. “that was my promise,” i say. “i did not know what happened.”"}, {"id": "R033", "response": "i stop moving and keep the scrap beside you. i tap it once with my thumbnail, then leave a faint impression where the loose piece slipped. i leave the routine intact, but the scrap feels smaller and more tentative. i keep the pile beside you until i find a smooth surface where i can leave the discarded piece alone."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "i put the piece on the shelf. the scrape goes back. i put the other piece on the bench. the scrape stays on the shelf. i do not say what happened."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "I put the scrap on the bench and leave the piece where it was. the mark comes before the whole thing. I put my thumbnail near the scrap and hold it still. the piece can stay in the same place."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "i tap the scrap, pause, and write the half-done part on the bench. i leave it on the bench, then check the other half. i leave the scrap on the bench, then check the other half. i leave the one that behaves."}]
